workItem: Establish associates/JV carrying value using Dataset V2
question: Do the audited consolidated Ind AS financial statements disclose a supportable carrying value for investments in associates and joint ventures, for FY2024, FY2023 or FY2022, that populates INVESTMENTS_IN_ASSOCIATES_AND_JOINT_VENTURES under dataset schema V2?
oneLineReason: In each of the three periods the audited consolidated balance sheet carries no equity-method investment caption, the complete Note 2.5 decomposes both investment captions exhaustively into Ind AS 109 measurement categories and reconciles to the rupee, and the statement of profit and loss carries no share of associates/JV profit — so no amount exists to report, and an omission is not a nil.
sectionsExamined: Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss (both documents)
Consolidated Statement of Changes in Equity and Cash Flows (fiscal-year figures used by the evidence chain; no associates line)
Note 2.5 Investments, complete, both documents, all three periods
Note 2.5.1 Details of investments, complete, both documents, all three periods
Note 2.6 Loans / Note 2.7 Other financial assets / Note 2.9 Cash / Note 2.10 Other assets (FY2024)
Note 2.11 Financial instruments — accounting policies and risk disclosures (FY2024)

equityMethodTest.indAsRequirement: Ind AS 1 para 54(e) requires investments accounted for using the equity method to be presented as a separate line item in the balance sheet; Ind AS 1 para 82(c) and Ind AS 28 require the share of profit or loss and of OCI of associates and joint ventures to be presented separately.
note25MeasurementCategories: fair value through other comprehensive income
fair value through profit or loss
equityMethodTest.conclusion: No equity-accounted interest in an associate or joint venture is recognised in any of the three periods presented.

candidateFiguresConsidered.whyNotTheLineItem: Aggregate of debt instruments (government bonds, tax-free bonds, NCDs, government securities) and minority equity/preference stakes measured at amortised cost, FVOCI or FVTPL. Contains no equity-accounted component; Note 2.5 decomposes it exhaustively.
Sum of the non-current and current treasury/portfolio captions; a portfolio total, not an associates/JV carrying amount.

Same objection one year earlier: the FY2023 portfolio total aggregates government securities, NCDs, tax-free bonds, certificates of deposit, commercial paper and fund units. It is a treasury portfolio, not an associates/JV carrying amount.
Same objection for FY2022: the comparative column of Note 2.5 totals the debt and fund portfolio, with no equity-accounted component inside it.

Minority stakes in Airviz, Whoop, Nivetti, Tidalscale, Ideaforge, Merasport, Global Innovation and Technology Alliance, plus venture-fund interests (Stellaris, House Fund II/III). All measured at fair value; none is described as an associate or joint venture, and none is equity-accounted. A financial investment is not an associates/JV carrying value.

The FY2023 list is the same set of fair-valued minority stakes and fund interests (Whoop, Nivetti, Ideaforge, Global Innovation and Technology Alliance, Stellaris, House Fund II/III); none is described as an associate or joint venture.
The FY2022 comparative shows the same fair-valued minority holdings; none is equity-accounted and none is named as an associate or joint venture.
A listed minority stake of 16,47,314 shares carried at FVOCI. No significant influence is asserted; FVOCI measurement is incompatible with the equity method.
Issuer-level total assets — not an investment carrying amount and not an investee figure.
Issuer-level equity, which the market-consistent bridge already uses indirectly; not an associates/JV carrying value.

candidateFiguresConsidered.source: not part of the audited consolidated financial statements
candidateFiguresConsidered.whyNotTheLineItem: Form AOC-1 is an annexure to the standalone financial statements in the annual report. It is not contained in the audited consolidated Ind AS statements examined here, and its figures (investee net assets, ownership percentages) are explicitly not the required carrying value even when present.

ingestion.reason: The evidence supports no amount for the line item: none is recognised, so none can be reported.
ingestion.nilDeclarationReason: Absence is not a nil. The nil grammar requires the filer's own wording that the item is nil, with filing reference and period; no such wording exists in the pages examined, and the line item is a reported (non-derived) item, so a nil cannot be inferred from an omitted line.

valuationImpact.why: Nothing changed: no dataset, no observation and no payload member was added or altered by this work item.

why: The control is an authorised requirement (180 calendar days from the source-evidence date), not a consequence of the carrying value being unknown; a completed investigation does not switch it off.
This work item is the action the control exists to force, and its result is now on the record: for this issuer the policy zero coincides with what the consolidated statements recognise.
No implementation defect was found in the control, so there is no basis to change the clock start, the 180-day age or the flag semantics.

notExamined.what: Notes 2.13 to 2.27 of the FY2024 statement (pp. 31-57), including Note 2.19 Other income, Note 2.24 Contingent liabilities and Note 2.25 Related party transactions (p. 50).
notExamined.why: The PDF text extraction available in this environment returns the first 30 pages of the filing (through Note 2.12.4).
notExamined.effectOnTheConclusion: None for this question. The conclusion rests on three complete primary statements plus the complete Note 2.5/2.5.1 reconciliation: an equity-accounted interest cannot be recognised without a separate balance-sheet caption (Ind AS 1.54(e)), a share of its result in profit or loss (Ind AS 1.82(c)), and its own reconciliation in the investments note. All three are absent, and the investment captions tie to the rupee.
notExamined.residualRisk: A related-party list could name an associate that the balance sheet treats as immaterial or dormant; that would not create a carrying amount to ingest, but it is a reason to keep L-036 open rather than to close it.
notExamined.resolvedBy: residualReview (2026-11-07): pages 31-57 of both filings were read note by note. No associate, joint venture, dormant associate or equity-method balance is disclosed, and the group-structure annexure that follows Note 2.25 has no associates block.

limitations.L-036: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — unchanged. The carrying value is not established as a reported observation, because the statements recognise none. This work item narrows the reason (evidence examined, nothing to ingest) but does not close the entry.
limitations.L-035: OPEN — unchanged. Nothing here weakens or strengthens the documentary-mapping limitation; no new nil declaration was made.

residualReview.trigger: The WI-4 record stated that Notes 2.13-2.27 could not be machine-read (the 30-page extraction window) and that a related-party roster could still name an associate. This review closes that gap.
residualReview.method: Both filings are digitally typeset PDFs with a complete text layer (they are not scans). Pages 31-57 were read through a full-document reader of the same PDF that does not truncate at 30 pages, page-anchored to the page numbers printed in the filed text. Every note was opened and characterised; the two notes capable of carrying an associates/JV disclosure (2.19 and 2.25) are transcribed in full in the bundle.
documents: INFY-INDAS-CONSOL-FY23 (pages 37-54, for FY2023 and the FY2022 comparatives)

pageCoverage.pagesRead: pp. 31-57 of the FY2024 filing; pp. 37-54 of the FY2023 filing
pageCoverage.notReRead: the interior movement tables of Notes 2.21 (leases) and 2.22 (employee benefits), pp. 41-46 of the FY2024 filing; their opening tables and closing pages were read
pageCoverage.whyItDoesNotAffectTheQuestion: Both notes reconcile balances the balance sheet and Note 2.11 already account for (right-of-use assets, lease liabilities, defined benefit obligations, share-based payment plans). Neither can present a third-party equity interest, and neither is a route by which an equity-accounted investment could be omitted from the balance sheet, the investments note and the group-structure annexure at once.

relationshipFindings.dormancyMarkersAttachTo: subsidiaries under liquidation (e.g. "(22) Under liquidation"; "Liquidated effective July 14, 2023"; "Liquidated effective November 1, 2023") — entities already consolidated line by line, which is the opposite of a dormant associate held outside consolidation

wordCheck.associateOrAssociates: no occurrence in Notes 2.13-2.27 other than the tax phrase in Note 2.24.1
wordCheck.quotedTaxPhrase: These claims are on account of issues of disallowance of expenditure towards software being held as capital in nature, payments made to associated enterprises held as liable for withholding of taxes, among others. (Note 2.24.1, page 48)
wordCheck.assessment: "Associated enterprises" is Indian income-tax terminology (transfer pricing and withholding on payments to non-residents). It names no entity, asserts no relationship, carries no balance, and is not an Ind AS 28 associate.

strictDistinctions.howApplied: Note 2.25 lists every related party. Subsidiaries are consolidated line by line; trusts are controlled or KMP-related; KMP are individuals. None is a related party that is also an equity-accounted investee.

strictDistinctions.distinction: dormant associate vs recognised carrying value
strictDistinctions.howApplied: The only dormancy markers are "(22) Under liquidation" and liquidation footnotes on subsidiaries. Even if one were an associate, dormancy would not create a carrying amount, and none is asserted.

strictDistinctions.distinction: investee's financial information vs Infosys's recognised investment
strictDistinctions.howApplied: The group-structure annexure shows each entity's share of consolidated net assets and profit — investee-level attribution, not an investment carrying amount, and only for consolidated subsidiaries.

strictDistinctions.distinction: transaction or balance with a related party vs the carrying amount of an equity-accounted investment
strictDistinctions.howApplied: The only related-party amounts disclosed are KMP compensation (130 / 127) and CSR contributions; both are profit-or-loss items, not balances, and neither is an investment.

strictDistinctions.distinction: absence of a disclosed amount vs an explicit nil
strictDistinctions.howApplied: Nothing in these notes says the associates/JV balance is nil. The finding is structural absence, which is why no V2 observation and no nil declaration were created.
